lessons.title: Can for Present/Future Ability and Permission
lessons.content: Can is used to talk about the ability to do something at a given time in the present or future. It is used to make statements about what is possible. Can is more informal. The structure is Subject + can + V1.

details.explanation: 'Can' is used to talk about current abilities and skills.
details.burmese: သူ အင်္ဂလိပ်စာကို ကောင်းကောင်းကျွမ်းကျင်စွာ ပြောနိုင်တယ်။

details.explanation: 'Can' can also refer to future possibilities.
details.example: You can take a holiday tomorrow if you want.
details.burmese: မင်းနားချင်ရင် မနက်ဖန်နားနိုင်တယ်။

details.explanation: 'Cannot' (can't) is used to express inability or impossibility.
details.burmese: ငါအရမ်းများများ မသောက်နိုင်ဘူး။

details.explanation: 'Can' is used for informal requests and asking permission.
details.example: Can you take me to the Victoria station?

details.explanation: 'Can' is used to ask for permission informally.
details.example: Can I borrow your car tomorrow?
details.burmese: မင်းရဲ့ကားကို မနက်ဖန် ငါ ငှားရမ်းနိုင်မလား။

lessons.title: Could for Past Ability and Polite Requests
lessons.content: Could is used to talk about past time ability. Could is also used as a polite way of telling or asking to do something. Could is more formal and polite than can. The structure is Subject + could + V1.

details.explanation: 'Could' is used to talk about abilities in the past.
details.example: I could run 10 miles when I was young.
details.burmese: ငါငယ်ငယ်က ၁၀ မိုင် ပြေးနိုင်ခဲ့တယ်။

details.explanation: 'Could not' (couldn't) is used to express inability in the past.
details.example: I could not take chilli when I was 12.
details.burmese: ကျွန်မ ၁၂ နှစ်တုန်းက ငရုတ်သီး မစားနိုင်ခဲ့ဘူး။

details.explanation: 'Could' is used for polite requests. It is more formal than 'can'.
details.example: Could you lock the door when you leave?
details.burmese: မင်းထွက်သွားရင် တံခါးခတ်ပေးနိုင်မလား။

details.explanation: 'Could' is used to ask for permission in a more formal way.
details.example: Could I choose my own doctor?
details.burmese: ကျွန်တော်တို့အတွက်ဆရာဝန်ကို ကျွန်တော်တို့ဘက်က ကိုယ်တိုင် လွတ်လပ်စွာ ရွေးချယ်နိုင်မလား။

lessons.title: Can vs Could
lessons.content: Can and could are both modal verbs used for ability and permission, but they differ in formality and time reference.

details.explanation: 'Could' is more formal and polite than 'can'. Use 'could' in formal situations.
details.example: Can you help me? (informal) / Could you help me? (formal/polite)

details.explanation: 'Can' is for present/future, while 'could' is for past or hypothetical situations.
details.example: I can swim now. (present) / I could swim when I was 5. (past)
details.burmese: ငါ အခု ရေကူးနိုင်တယ်။ (လက်ရှိ) / ငါ ၅ နှစ်တုန်းက ရေကူးနိုင်ခဲ့တယ်။ (အတိတ်)

details.explanation: 'Could' is softer and more polite than 'can' for requests.
details.example: Can I sit here? (casual) / Could I sit here? (very polite)
